note: Re-judged after TestRFC4754SignerPadsRAndS began forcing both short integers. RFC 4754 Section 7: the ECDSA-256/384/521 signature payload SHALL be r concatenated with s, 256/384/528 bits each, left-padded with zeros. Receive side: TestRFC4754SignatureIsRConcatS, through verifyRemoteAuth for methods 9, 10 and 11, accepts r||s with a padded short r and refuses s||r (errSignatureFailed) and the DER SEQUENCE (length); its records are line mutants of verifyECDSAAuth observed red. Send side: TestRFC8247LegacySignatureWithoutNotify drives computeX509Auth with no notify for each curve and requires method 9/10/11, exactly 64/96/132 octets, and ecdsa.Verify of the first half as r and the second as s with SHA-256/384/512, so DER output, a swap, a wrong hash or unpadded scalars go red. TestRFC4754SignerPadsRAndS loops computeX509Auth (up to 20000 tries) until it has seen both an r and an s below 2^248, requiring 64 octets on every signature, a leading zero octet on each short integer and a verifying r||s, and fails if either case was never seen, so a signer that leaves r or s unpadded goes red deterministically; the earlier s-padding gap is closed. Send-side tags are positive only; the negative polarity is the receive-side test.
